relevance_reason: The paper reports three consanguineous Iranian families with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome caused by novel homozygous loss-of-function COL9A3 variants. This is STL6.

findings.statement: Rad et al. (2022) described a 28-year-old Iranian woman (family 1), the only affected child of first-cousin parents. She had high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with empty vitreous, multiple lattice degenerations and retinal pigmentary changes, and severe progressive sensorineural hearing loss. One skull x-ray showed unilateral absence of the frontal sinus. Her joint and bone examination and x-rays were normal, although she had knee pain. She lacked the typical Stickler craniofacial features.
quotes: The female proband (II1) from Family 1 is the oldest and only affected individual out of three children from first cousin parents.

She suffers from high myopia in both eyes, in addition to vitreoretinal degeneration with empty vitreous, multiple lattice degenerations and retinal pigmentary changes. There was unilateral absence of the frontal sinus in her skull X-ray. She has severe and progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Typical STL craniofacial features such as midface hypoplasia, cleft palate, micrognathia, depressed nasal bridge and anteverted nares are absent.

findings.statement: Rad et al. (2022) described 2 affected brothers (family 2), aged 65 and 57 years, born to Iranian first-cousin parents. Advanced vitreoretinal degeneration caused recurrent rhegmatogenous retinal detachments that required multiple surgeries. The older brother had no light perception in either eye; the younger could count fingers with one eye and had no light perception in the other. Both had severe progressive sensorineural hearing loss and a herniated cervical disc. The older brother also had muscular atrophy.
quotes: Both had a history of multiple vitreoretinal surgeries due to recurrent rhegmatogenous retinal detachments resulting from advanced vitreoretinal degeneration.
Both suffer from severe and progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Likewise, both show a herniated cervical disc and muscular atrophy was noted in the older sibling.
the older patient is considered blind without light perception (NLP) in either eye while his sibling has counting finger vision for one eye while NLP was noted for the other eye

findings.statement: Rad et al. (2022) described 2 sibs (family 3), a boy aged 11.8 years and a girl aged 3.1 years, born to Iranian first-cousin parents. Both had myopia and congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing impairment. Both had spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, pes planus, a depressed nasal bridge and anteverted nares. Midface hypoplasia and downslanting palpebral fissures were more pronounced in the girl. The boy had knee pain. Neither had intellectual disability.
quotes: Both affected individuals have myopia and congenital moderate to severe progressive sensorineural hearing impairment.

X-ray and detailed examination demonstrated spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia in both children. Both individuals II1 and II4 have pes planus, depressed nasal bridge and anteverted nares, with midface hypoplasia and downslanting palpebral fissures more pronounced in II4.
None of the individuals showed signs of intellectual disability.

findings.statement: In the proband of family 1 with Stickler syndrome, exome sequencing by Rad et al. (2022) identified a homozygous 10-bp deletion in exon 2 of COL9A3 (c.107_116del, NM_001853.3), predicted to cause a frameshift (p.Pro36ArgfsTer49). Its allele frequency in gnomAD was 0.0000139 (2 carriers). The variant was not reported in Iranome, GME or 1000 Genomes. Segregation was checked by Sanger sequencing in available family members.
quotes: The proband in Family 1 was found to have a COL9A3 deletion (c.107_116del, p.(Pro36Argfs*49), rs1470627424), causing a frameshift in exon 2. The allele frequency in gnomAD is 0.00001390 with two carriers, while other public genomic databases such as Iranome and GME, and 1000 genomes have not reported this variant.
Segregation analysis using Sanger sequencing was performed in available family members to confirm variant segregation after PCR amplification.

findings.statement: In 2 affected brothers from family 2 with Stickler syndrome, Rad et al. (2022) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in exon 23 of COL9A3 (c.1204C>T, p.Arg402Ter) by exome sequencing of the proband. The variant was not reported in public databases.
quotes: The proband in family 2 disclosed a COL9A3 nonsense variant (c.1204C > T, p.(Arg402*), rs989413835) in exon 23
Both variants have not been reported in public databases.

findings.statement: In 2 affected sibs from family 3 with Stickler syndrome, Rad et al. (2022) identified a homozygous 1-bp deletion in exon 7 of COL9A3 (c.355delC) by exome sequencing of the proband. The paper reports the predicted frameshift as p.Leu119SerfsTer9 in the text and as p.Leu119SerfsTer10 in Table 1. The variant was not reported in public databases.
quotes: the proband in Family 3 showed a one base pair deletion in COL9A3 [c.355delC, p.(Leu119Serfs*9)] in exon 7. Both variants have not been reported in public databases.

findings.statement: Rad et al. (2022) compared their 5 patients with previously reported patients carrying biallelic COL9A3 loss-of-function variants, for a total of 7 families. Consistent features were moderate-to-profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss and moderate to high myopia with vitreoretinal degeneration. Retinal detachment and cataract occurred occasionally, and skeletal involvement was more variable. The older patients in family 2 had only myopia, hearing loss and herniated cervical discs, whereas the younger patients in family 3 had spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia and craniofacial abnormalities.
quotes: Consistent clinical features among STL patients with biallelic COL9A3 LOF alleles comprise moderate-to-profound progressive sensorineural hearing loss and moderate high myopia with vitreoretinal degeneration. Retinal detachment and cataract occur occasionally. In contrast, skeletal involvement seems to be more variable.

In summary, our report consolidates that homozygous loss of function variants in COL9A3 cause STL (type VI). We find high myopia and moderate-severe hearing loss to be consistent features amongst all cases while skeletal findings seem more variable.

findings.statement: Rad et al. (2022) observed no mild phenotypes in heterozygous carriers in their families. This differs from Nixon et al., who reported that carrier parents can show mild Stickler syndrome features.
quotes: Moreover, Nixon et al. [13] observed that carrier parents can manifest mild STL phenotypes, while our report and others have not observed mild phenotypes in heterozygous individuals.

relevance_reason: Reports a new patient with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome caused by compound heterozygous COL9A3 nonsense variants, with detailed clinical description.

findings.statement: Markova et al. (2021) reported a boy, born to healthy nonconsanguineous Russian parents, with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. At 1 month he had hip dysplasia with bilateral absence of ossification centers. At 3 months he had congenital high bilateral myopia. At 11 months he was diagnosed with bilateral grade 3-4 sensorineural hearing loss, and he had delayed speech. Radiographs at 1 and 3 years showed mild spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with spina bifida occulta of the sacral vertebrae, mild platyspondyly, kyphosis, flattened and irregular femoral heads, coxa valga, and flattened distal femoral epiphyses. Eye examination showed peripheral pigment changes, multiple vitreous floaters, and a preretinal membrane, with a normal ERG. At age 2 years 5 months he had genu valgum, waddling gait, lower limb joint pain, a flat nasal bridge, mild midface hypoplasia, a high palate, and no cleft palate. The authors considered the joint pain from age 3 years to be early-onset arthropathy.
quotes: At the age of 3 months, a systemic skeletal disease was suspected at the orthopedic examination and ophthalmologic examination showed congenital high bilateral myopia.

At the age of 11 months, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss grade 3–4 was diagnosed by a surdologist, and hearing‐aids were assigned. Further examination revealed radiographic signs of spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia.
Several dysmorphic facial features were presented with a slightly flattened nasal bridge, small nose, mild mid‐facial hypoplasia, high palate.

findings.statement: Markova et al. (2021) used targeted sequencing of 166 skeletal disorder genes in the boy with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. They found compound heterozygous nonsense mutations in the COL9A3 gene: c.268C>T (p.Arg90Ter) in exon 5 and c.1729C>T (p.Arg577Ter) in exon 30. Sanger sequencing showed that the mutations were in trans, and his healthy sibs did not carry pathogenic COL9A3 variants. The authors stated that this was the first reported case of COL9A3-related recessive Stickler syndrome not caused by a homozygous mutation.
quotes: Targeted sequencing of 166 genes associated with congenital skeletal disorders identified two undescribed heterozygous nucleotide variants in the COL9A3 gene: c.268C>T (p.Arg90Ter) in exon 5, and c.1729C>T (p.Arg577Ter) in exon 30.
Segregation analysis of the identified variants in the family by Sanger sequencing showed their trans‐position.
Moreover, we present the first clinical case not caused by a homozygous mutation with two novel compound‐heterozygous LoF mutations.

findings.statement: Markova et al. (2021) compared their patient with 6 previously reported patients from 3 families with recessive COL9A3-related Stickler syndrome. High myopia and sensorineural hearing loss were present in all patients, and none had cleft palate. Their patient also had early-onset arthropathy and vitreoretinal degeneration, which the authors described as a more severe presentation.
quotes: Congenital high myopia and moderately severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss from a very early age were uniform manifestations for all COL9A3 recessive STL patients, including the one in the present study.

All the described COL9A3 recessive STL cases were characterized by the absence of cleft palate, possibly being a hallmark of autosomal dominant STL forms where this trait is noted in 41% of cases [3].
Our case further expands the known phenotype with a more severe clinical presentation of an early‐onset arthropathy and vitreoretinal degeneration.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with recessive Stickler syndrome caused by a homozygous COL9A3 variant (2 patients), which bears on STL6. The abstract gives no variant-level detail.

findings.statement: Nixon et al. (2019) described 6 patients from 4 families with recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygous variants in Type IX collagen genes: COL9A1 (1 family, 1 patient), COL9A2 (2 families, 3 patients), and COL9A3 (1 family, 2 patients). All patients were highly myopic, with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel, and all had sensorineural hearing loss. One patient had severe arthropathy.
quotes: Six affected patients were identified from four pedigrees with variants in COL9A1 (one family, one patient), COL9A2 (two families, three patients), and COL9A3 (one family, two patients).
All patients were highly myopic with congenital megalophthalmos and abnormal, hypoplastic vitreous gel, and all had sensorineural hearing loss. One patient had severe arthropathy.

findings.statement: In 2 patients from 1 family with recessive Stickler syndrome, Nixon et al. (2019) identified a homozygous variant in the COL9A3 gene. Across the 4 families studied (with COL9A1, COL9A2, or COL9A3 variants), 3 of the variants were novel.
quotes: Recessive forms are rare but have been described with homozygous variants in COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 and compound heterozygous COL11A1 variants.

Six affected patients were identified from four pedigrees with variants in COL9A1 (one family, one patient), COL9A2 (two families, three patients), and COL9A3 (one family, two patients). Three variants were novel.

findings.statement: Nixon et al. (2019) noted that congenital megalophthalmos and myopia occur in both dominant and recessive forms of Stickler syndrome. Sensorineural hearing loss is more common and more severe in the recessive forms caused by Type IX collagen variants.
quotes: Congenital megalophthalmos and myopia are common to dominant and recessive forms of SS. Sensorineural hearing loss is more common and severe in recessive SS.

findings.statement: Nixon et al. (2019) suggested that COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 be added to genetic screening panels for patients with congenital hearing loss. Their reasoning was that early diagnosis of recessive Stickler syndrome would have a high impact for children at risk of dual sensory impairment.
quotes: We suggest that COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 be added to genetic screening panels for patients with congenital hearing loss.

relevance_reason: Reports the second family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to a homozygous loss-of-function COL9A3 mutation, the defining subject of STL6.

findings.statement: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) reported a boy, born to consanguineous parents (third cousins) from India, with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome. He failed newborn hearing screening and at 5 months had moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss on the right and severe loss on the left, which remained stable; temporal bone CT showed mild enlargement of the vestibular aqueducts. He had no myopia at 5 months, but by 2 years had myopia of -6.75 OD and -8 OS, progressing to -10.75 OD and -11.25 OS by 12 years, without vitreous abnormalities. Femoral and tibial bowing were present at birth. Radiographs at 6 years showed slightly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses, flattened acetabula, irregularity of the medial distal femoral epiphyses, and mild platyspondyly. He also had midface hypoplasia and no cleft palate. Growth and intelligence were normal, and autoimmune hypothyroidism was diagnosed at 10 years.
quotes: Audiology evaluation at 5 months identified moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss on the right from 250 through 4,000 Hz and severe sensorineural hearing loss on the left from 250 through 4,000 Hz.
However, by 2 years, he had developed myopia of −6.75 OD and −8 OS. By 12 years, this had progressed to −10.75 OD and −11.25 OS. No vitreous abnormalities have been noted.
Femoral and tibial bowing were noted at birth. Radiographs at 6 years demonstrated slightly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses, normal knee epiphyses, and mild platyspondyly (Figure 1).

phenotypes.text: moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss

findings.statement: In a boy with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome from a consanguineous Indian family (R08-308), Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) identified by exome sequencing a homozygous single-base duplication (c.650dupC, NM_001853.3) in exon 13 of the COL9A3 gene, predicted to cause a frameshift, premature termination, and absence of the gene product. The variant, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, was not found in public SNP databases; the unaffected parents and an unaffected sib were heterozygous. Prior targeted analysis of COL2A1, COL11A1, COL11A2 and specific exons of COL9A1, COL9A2 and COL9A3 had been negative.
quotes: In consanguineous Stickler syndrome family R08–308, exome sequencing was used to identify homozygosity for single base duplication c.650dupC in exon 13 of COL9A3 (RefSeq accession number NM_001853.3) of the proband.

The frameshift mutation predicts premature termination of translation and absence of the COL9A3 gene product. The nucleotide change was not found in public SNP databases, suggesting that it was unique to the family.
Genotyping of the parents and an unaffected sibling showed that all of them were heterozygous for the sequence change (Figure 2).

findings.statement: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) noted that all Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects (6 families, 12 cases with COL9A1, COL9A2, or COL9A3 mutations) had high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild to severe hearing loss, whereas vitreous and retinal degeneration had been reported with COL9A1 and COL9A2 but not COL9A3 mutations. They suggested that loss of the alpha-3 chain of type IX collagen results in a phenotype similar to that caused by loss of the alpha-1 and alpha-2 chains, and distinct from recessive COL11A1-related Stickler syndrome, in which hearing loss is severe-profound and cleft palate is present.
quotes: All of the Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects have exhibited high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild–severe hearing loss. Vitreous and retinal degeneration have been reported in patients with mutations in COL9A1 and COL9A2, but have not been reported in patients with mutations in COL9A3.

We suggest that loss of the α3 chain of type IX collagen results in a Stickler syndrome phenotype similar to that of the other autosomal recessive forms caused by mutations in the genes encoding the α1 and α2 chains of type IX collagen.
In contrast to patients with type IX collagen defects, the hearing loss is severe-profound. Midfacial hypoplasia and orthopedic issues have not been described.

relevance_reason: This is the first report of autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome caused by a loss-of-function mutation in COL9A3, which is what defines STL6.

findings.statement: Faletra et al. (2014) described the first family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to a loss-of-function mutation in the COL9A3 gene, a 23-bp deletion (c.1176_1198del) predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (p.Gln393Cysfs*25).
quotes: Here, we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family due to loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene.

findings.statement: Faletra et al. (2014) noted that Stickler syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. Dominant forms are caused by mutations in COL2A1, COL11A1, and COL11A2, and recessive forms had been associated with COL9A1 and COL9A2. They also noted that only heterozygous COL9A3 mutations had previously been reported in humans, in association with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 3, susceptibility to intervertebral disc disease, and hearing loss.
quotes: while recessive forms have been associated with mutations of COL9A1 (OMIM 120210) and COL9A2 (OMIM 120260) genes.

Up to this time, only heterozygous mutations of COL9A3 gene have been reported in human and related to: (1) multiple epiphyseal dysplasia type 3, (2) susceptibility to an intervertebral disc disease, and (3) hearing loss.
